name: Tomato
harvestHint: Pick when the whole fruit is one even colour. Fruit that has started to turn colour can finish ripening indoors at room temperature. Fully green fruit will not ripen. Above 32 C the red colour forms poorly, so fruit may stay orange in hot weather. The ideal temperature range given is for ripening.

name: Chilli
harvestHint: The first two pickings are green chilli. Later pickings are red ripe fruit. For dry or powder chilli, wait until the fruit is dark red. Wear gloves when picking.

name: Brinjal
harvestHint: Pick at the tender stage while the skin is glossy and smooth. Pick every 4 to 5 days. Do not let the fruit turn dull and hard.

name: Cucumber
harvestHint: Pick slicing cucumbers at about 15 to 18 cm long, and pickling types at 5 to 13 cm, while the skin is still dark green. Do not wait until they turn yellow and the seeds harden. Pick every 1 to 2 days. Below 15.5 C the crop matures late.

name: Green beans
harvestHint: Pick while the pods are tender, before the seeds inside bulge through the pod. Pods are usually ready about two weeks after flowering. Pick daily or every 2 days. Above 32 C the flowers drop. Days shown are for bush beans; pole beans take longer.

name: Mint
harvestHint: Start picking once the plant is 3 to 4 inches tall. Pinch the stems. Young leaves have the best flavour. Pick late morning on a dry sunny day. Leave about an inch of stem so it regrows. Grows in partial shade too. Always grow in a container, as it spreads fast.

name: Radish
harvestHint: Pull when the root reaches full size for its variety. Old radishes split and turn woody. Warm weather makes roots hot, tough and hollow. Keep the pot at least 6 inches deep and the soil evenly moist. The temperature range given is the germination range.

name: Green onion
harvestHint: Harvest any time once the plant is 6 inches tall. Cut the leaves as needed and they regrow several times. Keep the pot at least 6 inches deep. The 10 C limit is the minimum soil temperature for sowing.
